title: A Simple, Nearly-Optimal Algorithm for Differentially Private All-Pairs Shortest Distances

predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The proof in Appendix B chooses s = √n/(log(n)·√log(2/δ)). Tracing through the error calculation: the tree-based error term is O(√s·log^{1.5}(n)·√log(2/δ)·log(2sn/γ)/ε). Plugging in the value of s, √s = n^{1/4}/(log^{1/2}(n)·log^{1/4}(2/δ)). The √log(2/δ) factor in the numerator and the log^{1/4}(2/δ) factor from √s combine to give log^{1/2-1/4}(2/δ) = log^{1/4}(2/δ). Similarly, the Case B error also yields log^{1/4}(2/δ). Thus the overall error bound should have a log^{1/4}(2/δ) dependence rather than the stated √log(2/δ) = log^{1/2}(2/δ) dependence. The stated bound of O(n^{1/4}·log²(n)·√log(2/δ)·log(1/γ)/ε) appears slightly imprecise — the actual exponent on log(2/δ) is 1/4 rather than 1/2 based on the proof's own choice of s. However, this is a low-confidence finding because (a) under lenient strictness, a polylogarithmic exponent discrepancy does not affect the paper's core claims, (b) the Õ notation used in the abstract and introduction hides all polylogarithmic factors anyway, and (c) the main result of matching the Ω̃(n^{1/4}) lower bound up to polylogarithmic factors remains valid.

summary: Verification of 'A Simple, Nearly-Optimal Algorithm for Differentially Private All-Pairs Shortest Distances' (exhaustive mode, lenient strictness). The paper was segmented into 52 snippets across SECTION, DEFINITION, LEMMA, THEOREM, COROLLARY, EQUATION, PROOF, and TABLE types. 15 snippets covering the most critical content (main theorems, key proofs, contributions claims, and cross-section consistency) were verified in detail. Key findings: (1) The algebraic derivation in Lemma 4.3's induction proof is mathematically correct — the telescoping cancellation works properly. (2) Theorem 3.1's error balancing between the two cases (tree-based and input perturbation) is valid, with both cases yielding the same asymptotic n^{1/3}·polylog(n) bound when s = n^{1/3}/log^{2/3}(n). (3) Theorem 3.2's proof contains a minor polylogarithmic imprecision in the exponent of log(2/δ) — the proof's derivation yields log^{1/4}(2/δ) rather than the stated √log(2/δ) — but this does not affect the paper's core claims since Õ notation absorbs polylogarithmic factors and the matching with the Ω̃(n^{1/4}) lower bound remains valid. (4) Cross-section consistency checks confirm that theorem statements, abstract claims, and appendix proofs are mutually consistent. The paper's main contributions — achieving Õ(n^{1/3}/ε) error in the ε-DP setting and Õ(n^{1/4}/ε) in the (ε,δ)-DP setting, matching the known lower bound — appear mathematically sound. Overall verdict: PASS — the paper contains no critical errors that would require correction under lenient review standards.
